original_question: In the horocycle-flow example where M is a compact surface of genus g >= 2 with constant curvature -1 and sigma is the area form, so that the twisted geodesic flow on the level {H = 1} has no periodic orbits, do the sublevel sets {H < a} with a > 1 have finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Remark 4.3 (last sentence), in the specific setting of Example 4.1 (the horocycle-flow example), rather than the broader Conjecture 4.2.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right example and the right narrow issue from the paper: M is a compact surface of genus g ≥ 2 with constant curvature -1, σ is the area form, the twisted geodesic flow on the level {H = 1} has no periodic orbits, and the question is whether the domains {H < a} for a > 1 have finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity.
missing_details: The ambient phase space should be stated explicitly: the cotangent bundle T^*M equipped with the twisted symplectic form ω = ω0 + π^*σ, where ω0 is the standard symplectic form on T^*M and π : T^*M → M is the projection.
The Hamiltonian H should be identified explicitly as the standard metric Hamiltonian (kinetic energy) on T^*M; it is not an arbitrary Hamiltonian.
The phrase finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity should be made precise as c_HZ({H < a}, ω) < ∞ for the open sublevel domain {H < a} inside the twisted cotangent bundle.
The quantifier should be explicit: the paper asks whether each sublevel set {H < a} with a > 1 has finite capacity, not merely whether this happens for some a > 1.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should include that in Example 4.1 the flow on {H = 1} is smoothly equivalent to the horocycle flow and therefore aperiodic.

It is helpful to note that this is a separate, narrower open question from Remark 4.3, not the broader Conjecture 4.2 about neighborhoods of the zero section, almost-all energy levels, and low-energy contractible periodic orbits.
refined_question: Let M be a compact surface of genus g ≥ 2 endowed with a metric of constant curvature K = -1, let σ be the area form on M, let π : T^*M → M be the cotangent projection, let ω = ω0 + π^*σ be the twisted symplectic form on T^*M, and let H : T^*M → R be the standard metric Hamiltonian (the kinetic energy). In the horocycle-flow setting of Example 4.1, where the Hamiltonian flow of H on the regular energy level {H = 1} is smoothly equivalent to the horocycle flow and hence has no periodic orbits, is it true that for every a > 1 the open sublevel domain {H < a} ⊂ (T^*M, ω) has finite Hofer-Zehnder capacity, i.e. c_HZ({H < a}, ω) < ∞?
justification: The draft is aiming at the final sentence of Remark 4.3 in Section 4, which asks exactly this question in the hyperbolic-surface horocycle example. To make it self-contained, one must import the notation introduced immediately before Example 4.1: the twisted cotangent bundle (T^*M, ω0 + π^*σ) and the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian H. Conjecture 4.2 is nearby and relevant context, but it is broader than the draft, so the paper-faithful target is the narrower open question in Remark 4.3.
